newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OMB's Raines says Q4 GDP provides higher base.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OMB's Raines says Q4 GDP provides higher base.

text.p: Stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter U.S. economic growth will provide a higher base for growth this year, which will help efforts to lower the budget deficit, Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said Friday.

"Once the economy grows a little faster the base is now higher, so if you're getting two percent (growth) it's two percent on a higher base and that produces more revenue to the government and reduces our costs," Raines told reporters after testifying at a Senate Budget Committee hearing.

Gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the fourth quarter was reported at a 4.7 percent annual rate, which was higher than expected. President Clinton's budget forecast two percent GDP growth for 1997 and 1998.

"So any time we get one of these pleasant surprises, above trend, that's helpful," Raines said. "We certainly don't expect it to continue at that level, but even having it for a quarter or a half a year is helpful to the long-term," he said.
